subject: English
question_text: Read the following text and fill in each gap with a
stimulus: suitable word based on the information from the text.15=5 Eid is the main religious festival of the Muslims in Bangladesh. Eid means happiness. Everyone wants to share this happiness with their near and dear ones. So most of the people, who are living outside their homes for different reasons have a strong desire to get back home during the Eid vacations. As a result, there is a mad rush in the buses, trains, or launches for the home-bound people. This often causes transport accidents that take away many lives. However, it cannot stop people’s desire to meet their family, in-laws, or friends. What makes people rush for their homes in spite 3. of serious hazards? This is the pull of the roots. Do human beings have roots like the trees? The answer is ‘yes’ but unlike the roots of the trees they are invisible, they lie in our minds. It’s these roots that make a bond between us and family members, in-laws, friends, neighbours or even between us and the land where we were born and grew up. In that sense our families, land of birth, relatives, our culture, traditions, or surroundings are our roots. And wherever we stay, we have a continuous pull of our roots. It’s our roots that develop our identity making us what we are. When we lose that bond, we become rootless. Human beings who do not have any roots or contexts, are a non-entity. In other words, they do not have their own identity. Such persons are devoid of values, humanity, and social responsibilities. They don't know where they are from, and/or where they are heading towards. This often makes them feel empty and lost. Eid is the most important religious festival of the Muslims in Bangladesh. It means happiness. All (a) — their happiness with their relatives on Eid day. In our country most of the people (b) — out of their houses for different reasons. But they come home on Eid day to meet their family, relatives and friends. (c) — all the people go home, there is rush in buses, trains and launches. This often (d) — accidents. Inspite they come home for the (e) — of roots.
